decisions.decision_value: Design an original, trendy, and user-friendly television remote control
decisions.rationale: Corporate mandate to put fashion in electronics and fit interior design trends for TV remote controls only.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: we need design a remote control for television set, so, which has to be original, trendy and user-friendly.

decisions.decision_value: Selling price of 25 Euros and maximum production cost of 12.50 Euros
decisions.rationale: Project board financial targets to reach required profit margin.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: Selling price, twenty five Euros. That's for you. The production price, twelve and a half Euros, approximately.

decisions.decision_value: Lightweight material (unspecified)
decisions.rationale: Remote control should feel light in the hand.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: Only one thing uh that has to be added according to me is uh the the material it is made of, it should be something light.

decisions.decision_value: Younger consumers under 40 years old
decisions.rationale: New project specification from the project board targeting trend-sensitive young consumers under 40.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: with this new product we want to appeal to younger people, which are um the younger people were defined under forty.

decisions.decision_value: Corporate colours (black and yellow) and logo must be recognisable on the product
decisions.rationale: Mandate from project board to ensure corporate branding visibility.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: one thing that should be important is that the corporate l colour and slogan are recognisable, which is apparently black and yellow,

decisions.decision_value: Nokia-style interchangeable covers sold separately over a single base remote control
decisions.rationale: Allows manufacturing one basic remote control while appealing to diverse tastes and seasonal trends.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: why not just steal Nokia's idea and just make changeable covers for your I mean those cost hardly anything

decisions.decision_value: Universal television remote control working across diverse TV brands
decisions.rationale: As a standalone remote control manufacturer targeting a broad market, universal compatibility is required.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: I think we should go for universal, because apparently we're a separate company making separate c remote controls to sell to a lot of diverse people.

decisions.decision_value: Audio beep and flashing light locator triggered via a slap-on transmitter button attached to the TV
decisions.rationale: Users frequently lose remotes; combining beep and flash accommodates deaf users and works with universal TVs via a stick-on sender.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: We could make a combination that it goes beep and that you that some light lights up.

decisions.decision_value: Fewer, larger, fade-proof buttons for core functions (power on top, channel/volume triangles, mute, favourite channel, teletext) with advanced settings under a menu button
decisions.rationale: Users dislike cluttered remotes and faded symbols; 50% mainly zap channels so primary controls must be prominent and intuitive.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: So I think it should be have less or l very little buttons and maybe a second second level menu for the advanced things.

decisions.decision_value: Initially rejected LCD screen due to battery drain and cost, then reopened as provisional pending cost check
decisions.rationale: Concerned about high cost, space, and battery consumption, though marketing showed young users want an LCD screen.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: I think we should lose the L_C_D_ screen, like you said. I think for example it's it's huge I think the L_C_D_ is huge, it consumes batteries like hell.

decisions.decision_value: Rejected speech recognition in the remote control
decisions.rationale: Selling across multiple countries creates language barriers and speech technology was considered immature and memory-heavy.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: Speech recognition, I think it's very hard, because we're selling across multiple countries. So I think implementing speech recognition is such a small um apparatus, it's very hard to do.

decisions.decision_value: Rechargeable batteries with a TV docking base station or charging wire
decisions.rationale: Provides comfort and integrates with the locator base station on the TV.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: I think it's uh it's a pretty good idea to have uh like sort of a maybe a base station that you put on the T_V_.

decisions.decision_value: Basic regular batteries (rejecting kinetic energy, solar cells, and hand dynamo)
decisions.rationale: Rechargeable docking unit was not on the available component list, solar cells cannot pair with plastic/indoor use, and remotes lie still 99% of the time making kinetic shaking impractical.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: Well, mm it's not in the list. So we cannot choose from it. So

decisions.decision_value: Include an LCD display screen at the top of the remote control
decisions.rationale: Highly popular with the under-40 target group for technological innovation and menu navigation.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: because it is uh very hot in n our target group I think, we should take it take it t to consideration to build an L_C_D_ screen in it.

decisions.decision_value: Advanced chip with infrared sender
decisions.rationale: An advanced chip is mandatory to operate the LCD screen.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: Electronics, uh the first one is the chip. Uh that's no longer an option, it has to be an advanced one now. 'Cause we have the L_C_D_ screen.

decisions.decision_value: Include speech recognition (sample sensor and speaker component)
decisions.rationale: A new, compact speech recognition component became available and over 60% of surveyed users favoured voice recognition.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: Well, I heard that there was a new uh component speech recognition component, which was pretty much up to standard, so we might use that

decisions.decision_value: Rubber material for both the case and push-buttons (rejecting wood, plastic, and titanium)
decisions.rationale: Young consumers want a spongy feel, and rubber provides drop protection against falling.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: the buttons must a little bit spongy material. So uh rubber, I think uh th that's the best.

decisions.decision_value: Single-curve (banana-style) ergonomic profile with rounded corners and finger grip
decisions.rationale: Rounding off the sharp corners and curving the body fits the hand comfortably, aligns with the fruit/vegetable trend, and leaves room for internal electronics.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: I would curve the whole. Like um like it hangs over your hand a little bit.

decisions.decision_value: Rejected scroll-wheel in favour of standard rubber push-buttons (round keys, triangle volume/channel keys, square central menu key)
decisions.rationale: Voted 3-to-1 against the scroll-wheel because it takes up space, risks accidental channel scrolling, and adds no functional value.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: I don't think a scroll-wheel offers new functionality, whereas speech recognition and L_C_D_ screen do offer new functionality in your product.

decisions.decision_value: Yellow rubber cover with black buttons and corporate logo
decisions.rationale: Matches the black-and-yellow corporate identity while being flashy, banana-themed, and trendy for young people.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: It's either black cover with yellow buttons or vice versa. And I would say take a yellow cover and black buttons.

decisions.decision_value: Dropped speech recognition (sample sensor/speaker) from the final product
decisions.rationale: Initial prototype cost 17 Euros (4.50 Euros over the 12.50 Euro budget); speech recognition was the most expensive component (4 Euros) and had lower customer support (60%) than the LCD display (90%).
decisions.semantic_target_quote: What do we scrap. Well think I had the best solution that I came up with is just to s take out the speech recognition.

decisions.decision_value: Changed base remote colour from special yellow to standard black and grey, offering custom colours via separate interchangeable covers
decisions.rationale: Dropping speech recognition reduced cost to 13 Euros; removing the 0.50 Euro special yellow colour surcharge brought the final production cost down to the mandatory 12.50 Euro limit while preserving rubber and the 1-curve shape.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: I al like I said, I lost the speech recognition and I lost the special colour, which would make this black a black and grey.

decisions.decision_value: Named the product 'Triple R' (Real Reaction Remote)
decisions.rationale: Short, catchy name reflecting the company name Real Reaction; alternatives 'Banana remote', 'RC Deluxe', and 'Real Reactor' were scratched.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: I think we're all in agreement about the triple R_. I think triple R_ is cool.

disagreements.positions: Speaker A initially drew the LCD screen at the bottom of the remote, whereas Speakers D, C, and B argued it would be hidden by the user's hand and must be placed at the top because people read from top to bottom.
disagreements.semantic_target_quote: If you're reading from top to bottom, I think it's better to put it uh at the top.

disagreements.positions: Speaker C favoured kinetic energy provision powered by picking up the remote twice a day, while Speakers A and B argued remotes lie still 99% of the time and users will not shake their remote before watching TV.
disagreements.semantic_target_quote: Is that enough? Because I don't really see people shaking their remote control before using it.

disagreements.positions: Speaker C repeatedly pushed to include a scroll-wheel purely for flashy design appeal to young users, while Speakers A, B, and D opposed it as lacking functional value and risking accidental channel changes, voting 3-to-1 to exclude it.
disagreements.semantic_target_quote: It's not because it's functional, but it's just to add to the design, to have it flashy.

disagreements.positions: Speaker B designed a square remote with sharp corners and opposed building seasonal fruit shapes directly into the body, whereas Speakers A and D criticised the sharp 'Star Trek phaser' corners and insisted on rounded edges and a curved profile.
disagreements.semantic_target_quote: I think there needs to be a little I think it's too too sharp. The edges are too sharp.

disagreements.positions: To cut production cost from 17 Euros to 12.50 Euros, Speaker A dropped speech recognition and the special yellow colour; Speaker B disagreed with cutting the trendy yellow colour and proposed extending the budget to 13 Euros, Speaker D pushed to take a risk above 12.50 Euros because customers are willing to pay, and Speaker C suggested dropping the curve or switching from rubber to plastic, before Speaker A enforced the strict 12.50 Euro cap.
disagreements.semantic_target_quote: Well, I'd I tend to disagree with you on that, because the trend issue was a big issue when we started designing this.

disagreements.positions: Speaker D questioned what the LCD screen actually displays and whether it shows channel previews; Speaker A admitted video previews require too much bandwidth and that the team had not defined or utilised the LCD screen efficiently enough, resulting in a mediocre score of 3.
disagreements.semantic_target_quote: Yeah, we are using it, but it's not it's not poorly used, but it's not efficiently used, I think.
